sections.h2: Where do you take a deed for recording in Vinton County?
sections.html:
Vinton County deeds and mortgages are recorded at the courthouse, 100 East Main Street, McArthur, OH 45651. The recorder's line is 740-596-4314, and the county directory lists weekday hours of 8:30 am to 4:00 pm.

The same counter takes oil and gas leases, military discharge papers, and tax, unemployment and workers compensation liens. Staff will point you in the right direction, but they do not run title searches, help word a document or hand out blank deed forms. A seller who needs a deed drafted should go through a title company or an attorney before heading to McArthur.

sections.h2: What should a Vinton County seller know about the county itself?
sections.html:
Vinton County sits in the Hocking Hills region of southeastern Ohio. It was formed in 1850 from parts of Ross, Gallia, Jackson, Hocking and Athens counties, covers 414 square miles and has roughly 13,000 residents. McArthur has been the county seat since 1815.

No city exists inside the county line. The county's village page describes the landscape as more than eighty percent wooded and names four villages, with 2010 census counts of 1,701 for McArthur, 879 for Hamden, 278 for Zaleski and 149 for Wilkesville. Twelve townships make up the rest: Brown, Clinton, Eagle, Elk, Harrison, Jackson, Knox, Madison, Richland, Swan, Vinton and Wilkesville.

State parks, state forests and part of the Wayne National Forest draw outdoor visitors, and much of the housing stock is rural. Parcels cut from larger tracts are common, which makes the engineer's role in deed descriptions (covered below) matter more here than in a county of subdivisions.

sections.h2: How do you look up a recorded deed in Vinton County?
sections.html:
Older records and newer ones live in two places. Deed books and indexes from 1850 through December 31, 1985 are kept in the recorder's office. Indexes from January 1, 1986 forward can be searched on the county's Ava portal, though the online version carries names and index data without document images.

Current documents arrive on paper or electronically. The recorder's page says the office accepts transfer documents by e-recording and lists two submitters: ePN at 888-325-3365 and CSC at 866-652-0111. Homeowners can also sign up for the free property fraud alert, either at propertyfraudalert.com or by calling 1-800-728-3858, so an email or call reaches them when a document is filed against their parcel.

sections.h2: What does Ohio law set as the recording fee for a Vinton County deed?
sections.html:
Recording fees come from Revised Code 317.32, which pairs a base fee with a housing trust fund fee of the same amount on nearly every item. The first two pages of an instrument carry $17 plus $17, and every later page (8.5 by 14 inches or a fraction of one, caption page included) carries $4 plus $4. A county may add a preservation surcharge of up to $5.

The county's recorder page points to a new fee schedule and guidelines effective January 1, 2025, published through the Ohio Recorders Association. Before mailing a check, ask the office for the exact total for your page count.

  • Zoning resolutions filed with the recorder: $25 base plus $25 housing trust fund fee.
  • Zoning amendments: $10 plus $10.
  • Photocopies made outside the recording process: $1 plus $1 per page.
  • Certified copies: $1 plus $1 per page, with a 50 cent plus 50 cent charge for the seal.

sections.h2: Which Vinton County offices touch a deed before it is recorded?
sections.html:
A sale moves through several desks in the same building. The table lists the ones a seller meets, using contact details printed on county pages.

Vinton County courthouse offices in a home sale (county directory and auditor and treasurer pages)
OfficeRole in a salePhone
EngineerApproves deed and land contract descriptions, keeps tax maps740-790-7014
AuditorStatement of value, conveyance fee, transfers on the tax list740-790-7007
RecorderRecords the deed or mortgage740-596-4314
TreasurerCollects property tax, confirms what is owed740-790-7045
Clerk of CourtsCourt filings, titles and passports740-596-3001

In practice the order is engineer first when a legal description is new or changed, auditor second, recorder last. Handing the recorder a deed that lacks the auditor's endorsement will get it turned away.

sections.h2: What conveyance fee does the Vinton County auditor charge?
sections.html:
The auditor's site prints a conveyance fee of $4.00 per thousand dollars of the sale price, applied to real estate and manufactured home sales alike. The state sets a floor of $1 per $1,000 under 319.54, and a county may add a transfer tax of up to thirty cents per hundred dollars under 322.02, which is the grantor's cost.

The grantee files a statement of value under 319.202. It asks the seller whether the parcel carries a homestead-type reduction or farm-use valuation for the preceding or current year. If either applies, the two sides sign a sworn paper estimating the reduction or the recoupment charge and agreeing how to account for it. The auditor then endorses the deed with the fee collected and sends it on to the recorder.

sections.h2: Which Vinton County transfers owe no conveyance fee?
sections.html:
Section 319.54(G)(3) lists many carve-outs, and when one applies the filing states the reason instead of a value. The ones that come up in a county like Vinton include:

  • Transfers to or from the United States, Ohio or a local government body.
  • Deeds made only to give or release security for a loan.
  • Deeds that confirm or correct one already recorded.
  • Gifts between spouses, or between a parent and a child or the child's spouse.
  • Transfers carried out under a court order, to the extent no sale results.
  • Easements and rights-of-way worth $1,000 or less.
  • Transfers to or from a 501(c)(3) charity made without payment and for its charitable purpose.
  • Deeds among heirs or devisees of one decedent when no money changes hands.

A deed that moves property into a trust the maker can revoke at will is also on the list, as are the surviving spouse sales described in 2106.16.

sections.h2: What makes an Ohio deed ready for the Vinton County recorder?
sections.html:
Section 5301.01 requires the grantor to sign and then acknowledge the signature before a judge or clerk of a court of record, a county auditor, a county engineer, a notary or a mayor. That official certifies the acknowledgment and signs the certificate.

Recording matters because of section 5301.25. A deed goes on record in the county where the land lies, and until it does, the law treats it as fraudulent against a later buyer who paid in good faith and knew nothing of the earlier deed. When a survey was made of the land being conveyed, the auditor requires the surveyor's name to appear in the deed, usually through a line stating that a survey was made by that person.

sections.h2: How are Vinton County property taxes handled when a house sells?
sections.html:
The treasurer's page shows a 5 percent penalty added to second-half bills not paid by the closing date and a 10 percent penalty ten days later, citing ORC 323.121. For 2026, second-half real estate and manufactured home tax was due July 30. The treasurer accepts checks, money orders, cash and cards (a 2.75 percent processing fee applies to cards) and keeps a drop box in the alley behind the courthouse, which the page says should not hold cash.

The county's 2026 rate sheet for tax year 2025 lists 18 taxing districts. Residential and agricultural figures printed there include 34.280207 for Brown-Vinton, 43.440994 for Hamden, 43.551322 for Zaleski and 48.162418 for the McArthur corporation, each stated in dollars and cents per thousand dollars of valuation. A house inside a village therefore sits in a different district than one on a township road.

At a closing, the title company usually splits the year's taxes between buyer and seller by contract. If the bill has not arrived, call the treasurer at 740-790-7045 before the closing date.

faqs.q: What is the phone number for the Vinton County recorder?
faqs.a: Call 740-596-4314. The office is at 100 East Main Street in McArthur, and the county directory lists weekday hours of 8:30 am to 4:00 pm.

faqs.q: Can I e-record a deed in Vinton County?
faqs.a: Yes. The recorder says the office takes transfer documents electronically and names ePN (888-325-3365) and CSC (866-652-0111) as submission services. Paper filings at the counter are still an option.

faqs.q: How much does the auditor charge on a Vinton County sale?
faqs.a: The auditor's site states a conveyance fee of $4.00 per thousand dollars of the sale price. That covers real estate and manufactured homes, and the grantor pays it when the deed goes to the auditor before recording.

faqs.q: Does the Vinton County recorder prepare deeds or search titles?
faqs.a: No. The recorder's page says staff will assist where they can but will not search records, help prepare a document or provide recording forms. Use a title company or attorney for the drafting.

faqs.q: How can I be warned if someone records a document against my Vinton County property?
faqs.a: Sign up for the free property fraud alert at propertyfraudalert.com or at 1-800-728-3858. The county recorder offers it through its recording service provider, and alerts follow new filings tied to your parcel.
